value: Patients with alcohol addiction demonstrated lower volumes of GM than controls (patients: mean (SD) 569.4 (63.5) ml; controls: mean (SD) 631.9 (62.75) ml; p=0.002). Significantly reduced GM volumes were found in the thalamus, dorsal hippocampus, cerebellum, precentral gyrus, middle frontal gyrus and insular region. These findings support the assumption that alcohol dependence is associated with local GM dysfunction and suggest involvement of the anterior thalamus, posterior hippocampus, insular cortex and frontal cortical areas in alcohol-associated brain damage.

value: Patients with alcohol addiction showed lower volumes of WM than controls (patients: mean (SD) 435.5 (61.2) ml; controls: mean (SD) 470.1 (68.9) ml; p=0.085). Significant WM volume loss was found in the entire periventricular WM and reduced volume was found in the pons and cerebellar pedunculi. These findings support altered brain connectivity and are consistent with alcohol-associated degeneration of pontine, cerebellar and periventricular WM.
